title: Discussion: How to people actually use RPG Maker ?

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
I'll throw some wild statements into the room!
They are meant as a discussion starter (and therefore kinda incendiary), but I also happen to believe them. So it's not JUST provocation.
The overwhelming majority of video gamers have never even heard of rpg maker.
Without looking it up, most maker users couldn't tell you which general version (2000, VX, MZ ...) they are using.
Most maker users use only rtp ressources and PERHAPS randomly googled pictures, most likedly of the licenced kind.
Most maker users use none or only VERY basic plugins - and only if they are packaged with the programme.
Most completed rpg maker games have never touched the internet or been played by people unknown to the creators.
Most maker users have never interacted with another maker user, not even online. Only a fraction has ever visited an online community.
Most maker users wouldn't know who this "Alex" guy is.
All who do are now
officially old
.
Source? I said so!
It's just a little exercise about perspective.
Now, the thread title says "discussion", but I would actually very much prefer statistics. So if you have anything statistically sound that affirms or refutes these theses, please link it!
Also, discuss!

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
Thanks for the first answers, everybody! It's very interesting to see which statements are more strongly rejected.
The frontrunner seems to be
#2
, by a large margin!
Just to share my thoughts here, to help understanding: I can vividly remember our little high school maker crowd about ~20 years ago, and how much of a revelation it was realising that some of us had been using different programmes (2000 and 2003 respectively) for some time. I can also see a similar phenomenon when working with younger people today who tend to perceive "new hobby stuff" as a more generalised concept or brand. Extreme examples in video games would of course be long-running franchises like Mario Kart, FIFA or Pokémon: If you are new to these and not overly engaged, there is likely exactly ONE game you understand as THE Mario Kart, FIFA or Pokémon, at least for some time. This can even work for technology; a "Playstation" (no number!) is a very different console depending on who you are talking to, and in which country.
... but all of that might really be more of a thing for younger and less experienced people, and also for hobbies that do not have such a strong tendency to generate extreme engagement and focus from its hobbyists. So the statement might really be very wrong!
And since I should perhaps clarified the intention of this thread more clearly in the beginning ...
It's really just a thought experiment about perspective. If you are taking part in a hobby, much less treating it as a passion or a profession, it can be very easy to forget that you'll already have a very specific perspective on this hobby, and perhaps not even the most common or ""normal"" one.
Which isn't good or bad, it just is - and it is good to reflect on it!

ATT_Turan said:

Click to expand...
This is a fair point. But remember that like 90% of AAA games are made in Unreal, and that Unreal splash screen shows up a LOT. The brand awareness is really strong for even the most aloof gamer. Unity not as much, unless the user plays a lot of indie and/or mobile games.
But my experience is that the average user doesn't know $(&% from !@#$ about how games are actually made, even if said user spends all day on Twitter talking about how they'd fix gaming. Most people don't pay attention to the engine, or even understand what an engine is.
Anyway, my point is that I've seen discussions where one user will be like "I realized it's RPG Maker so now my opinion is negative" and then others will go "But game look like FF6 what mean?" RPG Maker is just a small community. So once you get out to the wide world you can see we're a small enough blip to fly under the radar.
